lesson_title: Why Your Balloon Sticks to the Wall
hook_text: A balloon sticks to a wall. But the wall has no charge at all. So what is holding it there?
clip_script: Rub a balloon on your hair and press it on the wall. It sticks. Two negative balloons push each other apart, and a negative balloon is pulled towards a positive jersey: like charges repel, unlike charges attract. But the wall is neutral. So why does the balloon stick? Inside the wall, the negative balloon pushes electrons slightly away and the near surface becomes a little bit positive. The wall is still neutral overall, but its positive side is closer, and closer means stronger. The pull beats the push. That same trick lets a comb pick up scraps of paper and a charged ruler bend a stream of water. Car factories in South Africa use it to wrap paint around car bodies, and power stations use it to pull ash out of their smoke.
visual_style: A whiteboard balloon on a wall with a zoom into the wall's molecules turning their positive sides towards the balloon, then two balloons swinging apart on strings, then a spray gun and a car body.
pacing: Quick puzzle, a slow zoom to explain, then a brisk real-world finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and predict attract or repel.
